CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Eugene Walker is a 61-year-old male with a significant cardiac history who presents today for routine follow-up. He underwent aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013. Patient reports increased fatigue that he attributes possibly to age or being drained at the end of the day. He continues to ride his road bike 20-30 miles but tires more quickly than in the past; previously he could complete 40 miles. After longer bike rides, he becomes very fatigued and must rest when he gets home. He notes that his friend Tyler, who is older than him, now waits for him during rides whereas he used to be able to beat Tyler. Patient is concerned about his cardiac valve since he is approaching 8 years post-surgery (was informed the valve would last approximately 8 years). His last stress test was September 9, 2019. He requested an echocardiogram from Dr. Lewis and reports no drastic changes since his last visit. He denies routine testicular self-exams but reports a small nodule on his right epididymis that he is not particularly concerned about. Wife and friends have observed pursed lip breathing during activity; he denies associated wheezing. He denies that his fatigue is depression-related and states he is generally a happy person. He sleeps 6-7 hours per night, which varies. He tries to work out in the morning and makes reservations twice a week for a 5:45 AM swim. He reports snoring slightly but wife denies any reported apneic episodes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports increased fatigue with exertion. Pursed lip breathing observed but denies wheezing. No depression.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013.

Vitamin D3 50,000 units on Sundays and 2,000 units on other six days. Clindamycin prior to dental procedures.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works and gives lectures; reports starting work at 7:00 AM. Cycles on road bike typically 20-30 miles per ride. Swims twice a week at 5:45 AM. Attempts to work out in the morning. Married. Does not attend follow-up appointments at Hopkins. Does not have routine cardiology follow-up.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Overall doing well. Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing observed, low exhalation phase, clear to auscultation, no wheezing. Genitalia: Right testicle with 2-3 mm palpable nodule, does not appear to involve epididymis or varicocele; left testicle normal; no hernia. All other portions of physical exam normal.

RESULTS
Lab work from 4/10/2021: Alkaline phosphatase 156 (elevated); total cholesterol 247 (elevated); HDL 66; LDL 166 (elevated); triglycerides 74; TSH 2.68 (normal); CBC unremarkable; vitamin D 94 (high end of normal). Last stress test September 9, 2019. COVID-19 vaccination completed with first dose on 1/15/2021 and second dose on 2/5/2021.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair status post. Patient doing well overall and currently asymptomatic. Not currently followed by cardiology routinely. Will order echocardiogram and stress test. Recommend follow-up with cardiology; Dr. Vincent Sanchez suggested as physician.

Elevated alkaline phosphatase level at 156. Could be related to liver but most likely related to bone health. Will check labs today with results sent through patient portal or phone call if significantly abnormal. Will order alkaline phosphatase and GGT.

Abnormal respiratory finding with pursed lip breathing. Patient has low exhalation phase on exam and reports increased fatigue. Cycles 20-30 miles regularly. Will order pulmonary function testing for further evaluation.

Right testicular nodule 2-3 mm with no hernia palpable. Referral placed to urology for possible ultrasound.

Preventative health. Patient fully vaccinated against COVID-19. Will administer MMR vaccine today. Shingles vaccine recommended; front desk to schedule for next month. Follow-up in one year for wellness visit, sooner if needed. Patient to call with any questions or concerns.
